profile.headline: Lead Software Engineer @ Cigna | Developing Scalable Solutions
profile.summary:
With over three years of experience as a Lead Software Engineer at Cigna, I specialize in Python programming, cloud solutions using Amazon Web Services (AWS), and software architecture. My work is centered on delivering effective and scalable technical solutions aligned with organizational goals.  

I am committed to leveraging my expertise in developing robust software solutions to drive innovation and efficiency. My focus lies in building well-structured systems, harnessing the power of AWS, and applying my proficiency in Python to solve complex challenges collaboratively.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Developing a rating engine in consultation with Homesite Insurance based out of Boston, Massachusetts. Established data pipelines by sourcing user input, manipulating and engineering data, and performing calculations on engineered data to produce desired output. Established QA tests against established rating engines to rigorously test new product. Deploying developed product onto AWS, working with lambda, and dynamodb

positions.title: Business Intelligence Developer Intern
positions.description:
Working with the Big Data and Business Intelligence Group, I collaborated to develop artifacts to transform and manipulate data for standard format for ingestion in HDFS. Performed numerous queries utilizing HIVE to find differences between data sources and files. Learned to work with Scala, Hive, Pig, and Tableau. Created Tableau Visualizations to fulfill KPI assessments. 

   *Utilized Python, HQL, Scala, Spark, and Pig to manipulate, query, and source data
   *Became well versed with HDFS environment and associated technologies.
   *Became familiar with Scala and Tableau

   *Learned to manage time efficiently and complete tasks without direct oversight.

positions.title: Python Developer
positions.description:
Contract role.

Working with the Data Science: Advanced Analytics Group, collaborated with experts from both DuPont and Dow to create a database to house research data utilized for statistical analysis by DuPont Data Scientists. Required in depth knowledge of data management practices, ETL, and common packages utilized for data wrangling/engineering tasks. 

* Utilized Python, SQL and Excel to perform data engineering/wrangling tasks.
* Sourced the data from Excel spreadsheets utilizing python. 
* Wrangled, Cleansed, Transformed, and Verified data integrity of numerous data sources
* Assisted in developing ETL process to automate data upload. 
* Worked to build a database system utilizing Oracle SQL and python

positions.title: Data Analyst
positions.description:
Contract role.

To assist with company acquisition, I utilized skills in Python, SQL (Microsoft SQL Server), and Excel to sift through, transform and analyze company data from payroll to professional field visits.I was tasked with answering pressing questions posed by the acquiring company and delivered by the current CFO. I worked with another team mate to efficiently develop procedures to answer the questions in a timely manner. 

* Constructing complex SQL queries to source data into proper format.
* Utilizing Python and Excel to clean and transform the data to meet business needs. Data wrangling with pandas, creating Vlookup tables, pivot tables, etc.  
* Identifying errors within the data, analyzing and reporting on them, and subsequently fixing them if   necessary. 
* Working on multiple projects between departments, mainly tasked with extensive ETL development to ensure that company transition occurred seamlessly.

positions.title: Principal Research Assistant
positions.description:
o	Assumed leadership of Dr. George Zimmerman's Stockton Forest Management research initiative. Managed the crew and maximized efficiency in collecting and analyzing data for long and short-term studies in Stockton’s forest management plan. 
o	This involved collection of spatial data; transect locations, canopy locations, etc via Trimble. Also involved collection of field data related to canopy cover, forest fuels, reproduction, etc. 
o	Created a Stockton Forest management database and continued to manage this database throughout my career at Stockton. 
o	Created a GIS map in ArcMap and ArcPro that contained all the spatial data collected during the field studies. Linked the field data to the spatial data for analysis.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
o	Consulted with a conservation organization based out of Kenya with advising professor Dr. Andrea Presotto. 
o	Used census data taken over the course of 20 years to create shapefiles using the coordinates provided in the data. 
o	Created an ArcMap displaying these shapefiles throughout Diani beach and used remote sensing techniques through Erdas to identify land cover and create shapefiles from the classification. 
o	Created a GLM to identify what land cover has the most influence on the distribution of the colobus monkeys throughout Diani beach. We then used this data to identify the optimal location for a wildlife corridor.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Statistics and Computers teaching assistant-I taught SAS programming labs to all students taking stats in the environmental science major. Covered topics ranging from analyzing z-scores to performing and interpreting results of a linear regression.

o	Performed work on tree Crews, pruning, shaping, and doing tree removals.

projects.title: Interactive Visual of Countries GDP to Population, Population Density, and Land Area
projects.description: As part of a personal project for Data Gathering and Warehousing, I web scraped data from two different websites containing information for countries GDP, GDP per Capita, Population size, Population Density, and individual land area. I merged all this data into a single database. I then created an interactive visual displaying the relationships between a countries GDP, Population size, GDP per cap, and Population Density. Attached in the link you will find my code along with the interactive visual and my interpretation.

projects.title: Predicting Outliers: Defaults on Loans
projects.description: The goal of this project was to explore and build a model to predict defaults on loans. The challenges were to accurately predict the minority class (Defaults) over the various other statuses of loans. The data set was extremely imbalanced, and I had to utilize multiple different feature engineering techniques to get the data in workable format. I chose to build 3 different algorithms to compare how each fared over the other when dealing with imbalanced data. For each of the 3 algorithms, I built a model for a non re-sampled data set, and a re-sampled data set where I over sampled the minority class. This was to explore how each model improved when utilizing a re-sampling method.
